rationale: Ontology workstream 2026-10-02, `exports` was a GAP for go. The construct is real — Go spec 'Exported identifiers', a capitalized first character — and it is a CONVENTION, so a grammar inventory cannot see it (the json lane's `exports` ruling was overturned for exactly that reason). MEASURED: script/m14/go-ontology-census.ts probe C1 over go-stdlib + cobra. Pins: package symbol -> each exported top-level unit (func/type/const), the structural evidence tier, the declaration line, and the NEGATIVE surface (unexported names, struct fields, interface methods, methods) so a widening of the predicate is a conscious act.

expectRelationships.comment: the symbol still EXISTS and is still a struct with a member: the fix removed an EDGE, not a symbol. GO38's contract (a local type is a symbol) is unchanged by this lane's ontology work.

forbidRelationships.comment: unexported: first character is lower-case, so the Go spec does not export it
a struct FIELD is a member of Engine, not a package-scope unit (F3 export-uniqueness invariant; membership rides contains)
an interface METHOD is a member, not a unit
a METHOD is a member of Engine, not a unit

capitalized and a SYMBOL (GO38 publishes a function-local type), but NOT at package scope: Go gives a name declared inside a function body no reach beyond that body, so the spec does not export it. The first version of this edge read the export ARRAY, whose predicate is `!ownerName`, and published this edge carrying `exportForm: capitalized_package_scope_name` — a claim the edge itself contradicted. Live on cobra/completions_test.go as two edges (UserCompletionTypeHelper, UserCompletionTypeAliasHelper) before the fix.
